sampling_model.design: Independent and identically distributed observational or fixed-randomization sampling from \(P\); the known benchmark \(b_a\) is conceptually distinct from the observational propensity \(e_a\).
sampling_model.treatment: A fixed finite action set \(\mathcal A=\{0,\ldots,J-1\}\) under consistency, conditional exchangeability, and uniform overlap.
sampling_model.overlap: \(e_a(X)\ge\epsilon\) and \(b_a(X)\ge\epsilon_b\) almost surely for every action, with \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}b_a(X)=1\) almost surely.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A fixed number of balanced folds is used. Conditional on each training complement, clipped outcome and propensity learners have uniform \(L^2(P_X)\) errors of orders \(r_{m,n}\) and \(r_{e,n}\); orthogonality makes the conditional score bias order \(r_{m,n}r_{e,n}\), and \(\sqrt n r_{m,n}r_{e,n}\to0\). Fold conclusions are combined by a fixed-fold union bound, not by asserting independence of overlapping training complements.

FangRidderXie2026 Theorem 2 gives the fixed-penalty Hessian Gaussian quadratic-regret law, and Theorem 5 gives the efficient doubly robust optimizer and quadratic-regret limit; the common submodel sets \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), hence \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\), and restricts rules to \(\{\pi_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\).
Orthogonal function-valued Z-estimators admit uniform Bahadur representations and simultaneous estimated-score multiplier confidence bands under high-level approximation and entropy conditions.
Neyman orthogonality and cross-fitting deliver root-\(n\) inference for regular low-dimensional targets under nuisance product-rate conditions.
Gaussian and multiplier couplings approximate suprema of empirical processes under complexity and moment bounds.
A nonzero second derivative under first-order degeneracy yields a second-order limit and generally invalidates the standard bootstrap.
Directional differentiability permits uniform inference for statistics of optimized value functions when the marginal-optimization map is not Hadamard differentiable.
Confidence-penalized policy choice yields a simultaneous reporting guarantee and a regret bound over a policy set.
Inverting simultaneous confidence intervals gives simultaneous inner and outer coverage of inverse sets across all levels.
A smooth embedded one-dimensional curve in Euclidean space admits a simultaneous sausage-shaped confidence region.

body.tldr: On the common regular finite-action benchmark-centered softmax subclass of FangRidderXie2026, with \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\) and \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\), every nonconstant maintained frontier has a uniformly regular divergence coordinate: \(\inf_{c\in\mathcal C}|dK(\theta_c)/dc|>0\). On any prespecified compact interior subrange of the attainable divergence range, the unique inverse \(c(k)\) supports the uniform fixed-divergence expansion \(\sqrt n\{\widehat W(\widehat\theta_{\widehat c(k)})-W(\theta_{c(k)})\}=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\{\phi^W_{c(k)}-c(k)\phi^K_{c(k)}\}(O_i)+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). A shared conditional multiplier band is therefore simultaneous in divergence and remains valid after any measurable choice from the plotted regular curve. The optimizer influence cancels from this fixed-divergence contrast. The proved foldwise replacement theorem supplies the same-sample nuisance and optimizer-path approximation needed for the multiplier law; set-valued inversion remains the constant-path or nonregular fallback, and the Hessian quadratic form separately calibrates \(n\)-scaled penalized regret.

project_justification.gap: FangRidderXie2026 proves efficiency and regret limits at a fixed positive preference and illustrates a three-arm commitment-savings frontier, but does not provide a simultaneous band indexed by attained divergence after inspecting the curve. Generic indexed-inference results do not establish the fold-specific learned-influence replacement along the same-sample implicit optimizer path, nor do they supply the softmax-specific uniformly invertible divergence coordinate.
project_justification.niche: On the common finite-action exponential-tilt subclass, feature identification, uniform interiority, smoothness, and curvature imply the exact path identities \(H_c\theta_c'=-g_c\) and \(dK(\theta_c)/dc=-g_c^\top H_c^{-1}g_c\). Unless the entire path is the benchmark rule, the last quantity is continuous and bounded away from zero on the compact penalty interval. This geometry permits regular inversion from divergence to penalty, while the identity \(a_c=cg_c\) cancels optimizer-estimation noise in welfare evaluated at fixed divergence.
project_justification.fill: For every prespecified compact interval inside the attainable divergence range, the note defines the unique population inverse with explicit reversed endpoint conventions and a measurable sample inverse, proves the uniform influence expansion with score \(\phi^W_{c(k)}-c(k)\phi^K_{c(k)}\), and calibrates its simultaneous band with the same multiplier draws used for the joint path. The foldwise product-bias, shrinking empirical \(L^2\) envelope, global argmax localization, totalized Hessian, covariance replacement, and conditional chaining arguments make the band implementable. Set-valued inversion is retained for a constant path, a failed regularity diagnostic, or a relaxed model admitting tangencies or multiple branches.

body.related_work: FangRidderXie2026 supplies the broader admissible-rule framework and its three-arm commitment-savings frontier. Its Theorems 1, 2, and 5 give fixed-positive-penalty efficiency, quadratic regret, and efficient doubly robust optimizer limits. This note does not claim their general continuous- or mixed-treatment classes: it works on the common regular finite-action benchmark-centered exponential-tilt/softmax subclass, where the faithful coordinate map is \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\) and \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). The advance is a divergence-indexed, post-selection-valid simultaneous welfare band and joint path inference under explicitly stronger path-uniform conditions. BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovWei2018 supplies a generic estimated-score multiplier architecture, while this note verifies its difficult foldwise same-sample-path replacement inputs. ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML supplies the cross-fitting and product-rate architecture, and ChenFang2019 motivates second-order calibration under first-order degeneracy. Eventwise set inversion follows the logic of RenTelschowSchwartzman2024 but is used here as a fallback rather than the primary construction on a regular nonconstant softmax path.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The regular divergence-indexed theorem is restricted to a prespecified compact subset of the interior of \([K(\theta_{c_{\max}}),K(\theta_{c_{\min}})]\); clipping outside the attainable range only totalizes the inverse and is not an endpoint inference claim. The maintained nonconstant softmax model itself has neither a population tangency nor a self-intersection because its divergence derivative is uniformly negative. Set-valued inversion is needed for the constant-path case, for finite-sample diagnostics that do not certify regular inversion, or after relaxing the identification and curvature conditions. Conditional multiplier validity still needs the declared fixed dimension, bounded outcomes and features, overlap, fixed folds, nuisance consistency, product rate, global uniqueness, uniform interiority, three-derivative smoothness, and positive curvature floor. The totalized Hessian is essential off the high-probability regular event. The results exclude vanishing penalties, weak overlap, growing dimension, adaptive sampling, nonunique optimizers, and claims of optimal tube width; penalized-regret calibration is not an unpenalized-welfare regret theorem.
body.honest_scope: The contribution is estimation and inference for a causal welfare--divergence frontier on a fixed finite-dimensional, finite-action benchmark-centered softmax subclass. Identification is taken as given. The headline is the uniform fixed-divergence influence law and its post-selection-valid shared-multiplier band, supported by a proved uniform inverse geometry and foldwise same-sample-path replacement theorem. FangRidderXie2026 covers a broader admissible-rule setting; only the common softmax subclass is compared, using \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\) and \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). The regular inverse result applies on compact interior divergence ranges of a nonconstant maintained path. The constant path and models with tangencies, self-intersections, or failed regularity use set-valued inversion and do not receive the smooth inverse limit. No result is asserted for continuous or mixed treatments, \(c\to0\), weak overlap, growing features, nonunique optima, adaptive samples, or minimax-optimal tube width.
body.interpretation: A planner can index the displayed curve by an interpretable divergence budget \(k\), rather than by the penalty \(c\). On every prespecified compact interior divergence range, monotonicity and the uniform slope bound produce one penalty \(c(k)\), and the shared multiplier band covers welfare simultaneously for all such \(k\). Consequently any measurable divergence choice made after viewing the plot inherits the simultaneous guarantee. The fixed-divergence influence \(\phi^W_{c(k)}-c(k)\phi^K_{c(k)}\) has no optimizer-coordinate term: movement of the estimated optimizer changes welfare and divergence in the ratio \(c(k)\), so enforcing the divergence level removes that first-order noise. If the population path is constant, or if a relaxed application permits a tangency or multiple branch, the reported object is instead the full set-valued inverse. The separate quadratic process measures penalized-welfare loss at the fitted rule on the natural \(n^{-1}\) scale.
